says: A call travels one line, from whoever asks to the software a person already has. Open a station to see what is in it, and keep opening as far as you want to go.

stations.name: Callers
stations.text: An AI agent, a developer, another program, or the person at this machine. No caller is special: nothing past the front doors knows which make of agent is calling.
stations.passes: a tool call, a command, or a person's decision

stations.name: Clients and Front Doors
stations.text: Thin clients hold no engine logic. They carry a call to the one engine on this machine. The front doors take it in: MCP, the REST interface, and the engine's own pages, where only a person approves, signs in, or publishes.
stations.passes: the call, and who is calling

stations.name: Kernel
stations.text: What is the same for every kind of system. One part decides whether a call may happen, one admits and schedules it, and one runs the compiled target step by step, with no model. A write is recorded before it is made and read back after.
stations.passes: one step of the compiled target

stations.name: Packs
stations.short: One for each kind of system
stations.text: The only code that touches a system. Each pack knows one kind of system and reaches the kernel through one provider contract.
stations.passes: what that kind of system understands: a request, a press, a command

stations.name: Target Systems
stations.text: The systems a person already uses. None is changed to suit the product, and none knows it is being wrapped. Only the pack beside it ever touches it.

shelves.name: Local Storage
shelves.text: Kept on this machine and nowhere else: the project's files, the compiled target, the ledger of every run, the vault of secrets, and the engine's own browser.

shelves.name: Foundation Crates
shelves.text: Types and small services that every other part builds on.

shelves.name: Shared Server Additions
shelves.text: The first release is for one person's machine. These parts make a shared server, and wait until after it.
